title.en: Earth, metals and plants; cattle, wealth and the rite

summary: The list turns to the earth and what comes from it: stone, clay, hills, mountains, sand and trees; gold and the other metals; fire, water and plants, cultivated and wild; and the animals of village and forest, for which the text writes its own verb: may they be fit through the sacrifice. It closes with wealth held and wealth to come, prosperity, goods and dwelling, the rite and the power to perform it, the aim and the reaching of it. Sāyaṇa glosses the metals (śyāma is black iron; loha bronze, copper and the like) and reads the last items as possessions and the means of reaching what is desired.

words.context: joins each item to the list (Sāyaṇa on the first anuvāka: समुच्चयार्थः)
with kalpatām, which Sāyaṇa supplies from anuvāka 10: ‘may it be ready for me’

sandhi.rule: visarga before c becomes ś (P. 8.3.34, 8.4.40); so parvatāś, sikatāś, vanaspatayaś ca

samasa.meaning: lord of the wood, a forest tree

vyakarana.note: Nom. sg. of the n-stem aśman (m.): the n is lost and the vowel lengthened (aśmā).
The first member vanas- is probably an old genitive of vana, kept inside the compound (Monier-Williams; compare bṛhas-pati). Nom. pl. of the i-stem pati with guṇa (-ay-aḥ).
Enclitic me (for mama / mahyam). Sāyaṇa supplies the verb kalpatām from anuvāka 10 to these items; this anuvāka writes its own verb only once, in unit 4 (yajñena kalpantām).

translation.literal: Stone and for me, clay and for me, hills and for me, mountains and for me, sand and for me, forest trees and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May stone be mine, and clay, hills and mountains, sand, and the trees of the forest.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa treats this yajus as clear: «अश्मादयः प्रसिद्धाः», stone and the rest are well known.

words.context: Sāyaṇa: कांस्यताम्रादि, bronze, copper and the like

sandhi.rule: final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra, written as the nasal of the next consonant’s class (ñ before c; P. 8.3.23, 8.4.59); so sīsañ, śyāmañ, lohañ ca
final e absorbs a following a, which the text marks with the avagraha (eṅaḥ padāntād ati, P. 6.1.109); then visarga before c becomes ś. So also me ’gniś ca

me ’gniḥ as me ’yaḥ above; and the last me, before āpaḥ (the first word of the next unit), becomes ma: final e before a vowel becomes ay (P. 6.1.78), and the y is dropped (P. 8.3.19), leaving the hiatus

vyakarana.note: Nom. sg. of the neuter s-stem ayas; hence ayaś ca.
Nom. sg. of the neuter s-stem trapus, which Monier-Williams cites for this passage (beside trapu); hence trapuś ca, not trapu ca.
A neuter adjective, ‘the dark’, standing for a metal; Sāyaṇa supplies the noun: black iron.

translation.literal: Gold and for me, metal and for me, lead and for me, tin and for me, the dark [metal] and for me, copper and for me, fire and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May gold be mine, and metal, lead and tin, black iron, copper and bronze, and fire.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa glosses two of the metals: śyāma is black iron («श्यामं कृष्णायसम्»), and loha is bronze, copper and the like («लोहं कांस्यताम्रादि»). Gold, ayas, lead and tin are covered by his note on the first unit, «अश्मादयः प्रसिद्धाः»; fire and what follows it he calls well known in the same way («अग्न्यादयः प्रसिद्धाः»).

flags.note: ayas is ‘metal, iron’ in the dictionaries. Since Sāyaṇa makes śyāma black iron, ayas here is perhaps metal in general or a particular metal he does not name; he does not gloss it.
loha is ‘red metal, copper’ in the dictionaries; Sāyaṇa widens it to bronze, copper and the like. The readable translation gives his reading.

words.meaning: what ripens in ploughed land, cultivated crops
what ripens in unploughed land, what grows wild

sandhi.rule: visarga before c becomes ś (P. 8.3.34, 8.4.40); so vīrudhaś, oṣadhayaś ca
final e before a vowel becomes ay (P. 6.1.78), and the y is dropped (P. 8.3.19), leaving the hiatus
final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra, written as the nasal of the next consonant’s class (ñ before c; P. 8.3.23, 8.4.59). The pañcāśat mark [9] follows this ca; no sandhi across it
final e absorbs a following a, which the text marks with the avagraha (eṅaḥ padāntād ati, P. 6.1.109); then m before c becomes ñ

samasa.type: saptamī-tatpuruṣa, its first member a nañ compound
samasa.meaning: ripening in unploughed ground, growing wild

vyakarana.note: Nom. pl. of ap (f.) ‘water’, used in the plural; the vowel is lengthened in the strong cases (āpaḥ).
kṛṣṭa ‘ploughed’ (past participle of √kṛṣ) + pacya ‘to be ripened, ripening’ (√pac); the form is one of those Pāṇini lists by name (P. 3.1.114). Neuter, standing for the crop.

translation.literal: Waters and for me, plants and for me, herbs and for me, what ripens in ploughed land and for me, what ripens in unploughed land and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May the waters be mine, and plants and herbs, the crops of ploughed land and what grows unploughed.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa does not gloss these items: they fall under his «अग्न्यादयः प्रसिद्धाः», fire and the rest are well known.

flags.note: corrections.json, C5.3: the second witness reads अक्षिष्टपच्य; it is a W2 error. The text keeps अकृष्टपच्यम्, the pair to kṛṣṭapacyam.

words.meaning: by the sacrifice, through the sacrifice
words.context: Sāyaṇa: निमित्तीभूतेन, the sacrifice being the cause

words.gram: verb, root kṛp (kḷp; 1st class, Ā.), imperative 3rd pl.
words.meaning: may they be fit, may they be ready
words.context: Sāyaṇa: समर्था भवन्तु, may they be capable

sandhi.rule: visarga before c becomes ś (P. 8.3.34, 8.4.40); so āraṇyāś ca
-aḥ / -āḥ before a vowel: the visarga becomes y (P. 8.3.17), which is dropped (P. 8.3.19), leaving the hiatus
final m before v (vittam, the first word of the next unit) becomes the nasal of the next sound, a nasalised v, which the Taittirīya text writes व्ँ (P. 8.4.58–59)

vyakarana.note: Stands once, between the two adjectives, and serves both: grāmyāḥ … paśavaḥ and āraṇyāḥ [paśavaḥ]. Nom. pl. of the u-stem paśu with guṇa (-av-aḥ).
This second ca has no me after it: the text runs on from āraṇyāḥ ca to yajñena kalpantām. It is analysed as it stands.

Imperative (loṭ) 3rd pl. ātmanepada of √kṛp ‘to be fit, to be in order’ (the r becomes l, P. 8.2.18). The plural agrees with the animals. It is the only verb written in anuvākas 4–6; for every other item Sāyaṇa supplies the singular kalpatām from anuvāka 10.
Instrumental of means or cause: Sāyaṇa reads it as the cause (निमित्तीभूतेन).

translation.literal: The domestic and for me animals, the wild [animals] and: through the sacrifice may they be fit.
translation.readable: May the animals of the village and of the forest be mine, made fit through the sacrifice.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: «ग्राम्यारण्यपशवो यज्ञेन निमित्तीभूतेन कल्पन्तां समर्था भवन्तु» — may the animals of the village and of the forest, with the sacrifice as the cause, be capable.
units.reflection: Here, for once, the text names the means as well as the thing wanted: the animals are to be made fit through the sacrifice.

words.meaning: what is found or acquired, wealth

words.context: Sāyaṇa: sons and others, endowed with prosperity
Sāyaṇa: one’s own prosperity and the like
Sāyaṇa: निवाससाधनं गवादिकम्, cattle and the like, the means of a settled life
Sāyaṇa: निवासाधारो गृहादि, the house and the like, where one dwells

sandhi.rule: final m before a consonant becomes anusvāra, written as the nasal of the next consonant’s class (ñ before c; P. 8.3.23, 8.4.59); so bhūtañ ca
visarga before c becomes ś (P. 8.3.34, 8.4.40); so bhūtiś, vasatiś ca

vyakarana.note: Past participle of √vid ‘find’ used as a noun, beside the action noun vitti; likewise bhūta / bhūti from √bhū.

translation.literal: Wealth and for me, gain and for me, what has come to be and for me, prosperity and for me, goods and for me, dwelling and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May wealth be mine, and gain to come; what has come to be and prosperity, goods and a dwelling.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa pairs the items. Vitta is what was gained before, vitti «भाविलाभः», gain to come. Bhūta is sons and others endowed with prosperity («पुत्रादिकम्»), bhūti one’s own prosperity. Vasu is the means of a settled life, cattle and the like («निवाससाधनं गवादिकम्»), and vasati the dwelling that supports it, the house and the like («वसतिर्निवासाधारो गृहादि»).

flags.note: The witness of Sāyaṇa is damaged at two glosses here (पूर्वलव्धम् for -labdham; स्वकीबमैश्वर्यादिकम्, apparently for svakīyam aiśvaryādikam); the sense is reported in English and those words are not quoted.

words.context: Sāyaṇa: the agnihotra and other rites
Sāyaṇa: the capacity to perform them
Sāyaṇa: एतव्यं, what is to be gone to, the happiness to be reached
Sāyaṇa: अयनम्, going, the means of reaching what is desired
Sāyaṇa: attainment (the gloss is damaged in the witness)

sandhi.rule: visarga before c becomes ś (P. 8.3.34, 8.4.40); so arthaś, emaś, itiś, gatiś ca
final e absorbs a following a, which the text marks with the avagraha (eṅaḥ padāntād ati, P. 6.1.109)
final e before a vowel becomes ay (P. 6.1.78), and the y is dropped (P. 8.3.19), leaving the hiatus; so ma itiḥ

vyakarana.note: Nom. sg. of the neuter n-stem karman (the n is lost: karma); hence karma ca.
From √i ‘go’. The text has emaḥ (emaś ca), and Sāyaṇa reads it so; the dictionaries list ema / eman ‘course, way’ as neuter.
A feminine action noun from √i ‘go’, ‘going’ — not the particle iti; hence the visarga (itiś ca).

translation.literal: Act and for me, power and for me, aim and for me, course and for me, going and for me, attainment and for me [may they be ready].
translation.readable: May the rite be mine, and the power to perform it; my aim, the goal I move toward, the going, and the reaching.

units.traditional: Sāyaṇa: karma is the agnihotra and other rites («कर्माग्निहोत्रादिकम्»), and śakti the capacity to perform them. Artha is a particular aim («प्रयोजनविशेषः»); ema what is to be gone to, the happiness to be reached («एम एतव्यं प्राप्तव्य सुखम्»); iti the going, the means of reaching what is desired («इतिरयनमिष्टप्राप्त्युपायः»). His gloss on gati is damaged in the witness («गति रेष्ठप्राप्तिः»); it appears to mean the attainment of what is desired.

flags.note: emaḥ: the gender is not secure. The text has a nominative in -aḥ, which points to a masculine ema (or a neuter s-stem emas); Monier-Williams gives ema and eman as neuter.
Sāyaṇa’s gloss on gati is damaged in the witness (गति रेष्ठप्राप्तिः); ‘attainment of what is desired’ (as in his gloss on iti) is the likely sense but is not certain.
